findings.claim: frontend-deps now rejects a single glob COPY of the npm manifest files before npm ci, although in this project the glob can match only package.json and package-lock.json, the two files the rule allows (git ls-tree of starter/frontend at this head lists no other package* entry; the build-time glob match itself is inferred, not run with an engine). The message then says "source copied earlier makes every source change install everything again", which is false for that form and would send a learner hunting for a non-existent mistake (critic run on a copy of a private solution, one-line change). The README names the two files, so the explicit form is what the lab teaches; this is a valid-form rejection like cg-sme-containers-007.
findings.recommendation: Accept a source word whose glob matches only manifest names (for example, expand it against the frontend folder), or say in the README and message that the two files must be named explicitly.

findings.claim: compose-ports checks only ports entries, so a db service set to host network mode with no ports entry passes all compose rules (critic run on a copy of a private solution; first seen in the first pass, not reported then). The Docker host network driver page says a host-mode container shares the host's networking namespace, its application is available on the host's IP address, and publish options are ignored; so the 127.0.0.1-only intent the README states for published ports is bypassed, and runbook-run-env already rejects the equivalent docker run host-network option as "reachable from the network", so the two rules disagree. Inferred, not run with an engine: the db would also leave the Compose network, so the api could no longer reach it by service name, which compose-url does not notice. Low: an unlikely edit.

evidence.section: Host network driver: introduction and note on published ports

findings.recommendation: Reject network_mode host (and any non-default network_mode) on both services in compose-ports, with the same message runbook-run-env uses.
